A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NarrativeTrack work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Appendix Sections 7–11 in v3 correspond to Appendices A–E in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations of 20 MLLMs, pipeline validation, human annotation assessments, and supplementary ablations and controlled experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–5, Table 2, and Appendix E, including pipeline validation and benchmark control experiments.

M1.justification: Both retain the same ensemble detection, OSNet and face-recognition tracking, majority verification, Gemini contextual recognition, CRP templates, and GPT-4o/human QA refinement. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both use 1,006 QA pairs from 406 clips sourced from AVA, Video-MME, and LVBench. Human-entity coverage, reasoning dimensions, temporal scenarios, and text-only/reversed-video controls are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 13 open-source and seven proprietary models, including the additional 20-frame GPT-4o condition. Comparator membership in the pipeline evaluations and supplementary Tables 10–12 also matches.

E3.justification: Both use exact-match accuracy, 20 frames for open-source models, and 128 frames for proprietary models, with a 20-frame GPT-4o comparison. Frame-density settings, annotation samples, conditional evaluations, and likelihood-based evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The model-size, temporal-direction, continuity, distractor, frame-density, and perceptual-control analyses are retained. Text-only, reversed-video, likelihood-based, and qualitative failure analyses also match; v3 Section 11 becomes v4 Appendix E.

E5.justification: The triple-annotator assessment, Fleiss' kappa of 0.767, and plotted error bars are unchanged. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and findings are unchanged. Table 2 retains Gemini-2.5-Pro's 83.80% average; Table 11 retains GPT-4o's 72.27%, text-only 41.75%, and reversed-video 62.92%. Other tables, plots, and qualitative outcomes also match.

T1.justification: The entity representation, detection-consensus expression, greedy matching and recall definitions, and likelihood-scoring formula are mathematically unchanged. Equation 1 becomes Equation 3.1 through renumbering; no assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, CRP framework, automated-pipeline contribution, and temporal–perceptual trade-off claims. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the human-only applicability boundary, explanations of directional bias and perceptual confusion, limitations of model/frame scaling, and proposed future architectural directions. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, detector thresholds, model choices, prompts, QA templates, and filtering instructions match. The same code and dataset addresses remain; their relocation and the change from 'Project Page' to 'Code' do not establish changed resource availability.

R1.justification: The same 55 cited works and research-positioning arguments are retained, including the comparison with VELOCITI. Numbered citations become author-year citations, with bibliographic formatting changes rather than added or removed literature.

P1.justification: Prose and section order are essentially unchanged. Analysis and QA-filtering paragraphs gain numbered subsections, appendices become A–E, and citation style changes. Section 4.1's updated frame-density reference incorrectly points to Section 5.1 instead of 5.4.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different layout with a shaded branded title/abstract block, wider text area, new typography, and widespread resizing and repositioning. All 12 figures and 12 tables remain; previously fragmented QA-template Tables 5–9 now each occupy a single page.

improvement.justification: Keeping QA-template Tables 5–9 on individual pages and adding specific analysis/filtering subsections makes the retained material easier to consult. This provides a limited presentation improvement while scientific evidence remains unchanged. The newly incorrect frame-density cross-reference in Section 4.1 is a small editorial drawback.
